headline: LLM-driven extraction of chemical-effect evidence from toxicology literature
label: Llm Literature Curation Pipelines
summary: Corpus-scale LLM pipelines now convert toxicology full texts into structured chemical-effect evidence, with human-AI review in one design.
synthesis: The common thread across these three preprints is LLM-based extraction of structured evidence from biomedical literature, applied here to toxicology. AOP-Smart-Finder pairs LLMs with retrieval-augmented generation in a human-AI hybrid framework to mine large literature corpora for biological events, key event relationships, and AOP evidence. AOPTK is an open-source Python toolkit for LLM-assisted retrieval and extraction of chemical-effect relationships from toxicological literature. The third preprint describes an automated, continuous LLM-driven pipeline that mines PubMed/PMC full texts into a hepatotoxicity knowledge base of 189,212 findings across 17,002 chemicals. What is new is continuous, corpus-scale curation of literature into structured evidence, with human review retained in the hybrid design. The items do not establish comparative performance across these tools.
